findings: The CFTC Market Participants Division responded to a request from Coinbase Financial Markets, Inc. (CFM), a registered futures commission merchant.
CFM's described route is CFM to Coinbase Bermuda Limited (CBBM) to Deribit FZE, for specified foreign futures, foreign options and Deribit perpetual products.
The referenced March 2026 SEC/CFTC digital-commodity interpretation expressly lists XRP as an example of a digital commodity.

CFM represented that it would accept customer-owned digital commodities and payment stablecoins, including BTC and ETH, as margin from 30.7 customers; the letter's digital-commodity definition is broader than those two examples.

The staff no-action position conditionally permits the described transfer and right of re-use of customer-owned digital commodities/payment stablecoins for the specified customer foreign futures/options obligations.
CFM represented that Deribit would maintain assets equal to 100% of net liquidating equity for the relevant 30.7 customers in one or more accounts at Coinbase Custody Trust Company, LLC.

The letter requires, among other things, wholly owned affiliate status, a qualifying acknowledgement agreement, audit/SOC 2 disclosure, integrated risk oversight, local-law authorization for re-use, customer disclosures, use solely for specified margin obligations, and compliance with Staff Letter 26-05.
caveats: This is a staff interpretation/no-action position, not a generally applicable rule or Commission order.
The letter is expressly non-binding on the Commission and may be modified, suspended or terminated.
The letter does not prove XRP was accepted in a live CFM customer account, posted as collateral, re-used, or held in any specific quantity.
CFM's stated plan and the regulatory pathway must be separated from actual product launch, customer eligibility, venue configuration and posted collateral.

findings: Deribit's cross-collateral specification lists XRP as a cross-collateral currency.
The displayed XRP haircut is 15% for cross-collateral standard margin (X:SM); the portfolio-margin (X:PM) column displays no haircut.
Cross-collateral currencies can support margin for derivative positions with different settlement currencies.
If a settlement-currency equity becomes sufficiently negative, Deribit can rebalance by using positive-equity currencies to purchase the negative-equity currency.
Rebalancing is separate from liquidation; a default 0.05% daily collateral fee applies while a currency equity remains negative.
caveats: Venue-wide eligibility is not proof that every jurisdiction, account class or Coinbase FCM customer route can post XRP.
The current public schedule does not disclose actual XRP collateral balances or customer-specific use.
Rebalancing creates a possible XRP-to-settlement-currency conversion channel when XRP is held with positive equity and another currency becomes negative; actual conversions and volumes are unknown.

findings: RLUSD became available for trading and management on Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and Coinbase Retail.
Deposits and withdrawals are supported across XRPL, Base and Ethereum.
Ripple says it will provide liquidity to support RLUSD growth on Base.
Coinbase Global Exchange availability, including RLUSD collateral use, was announced as a future step rather than a live capability on the announcement date.
caveats: RLUSD listing and network support do not prove XRP is the settlement asset in each transfer.
The future collateral announcement must not be recorded as live collateral acceptance without a later operational confirmation.

causal_hypotheses.thesis: XRP eligibility in derivatives collateral systems and growing custody/distribution could increase institutional holding demand, liquidity depth and inventory requirements.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: No verified CFM customer XRP collateral balances
No disclosed net XRP spot purchases attributable to the collateral pathway
RLUSD availability is not equivalent to XRP collateral use
decisive_missing_data: CFM product-specific collateral schedules and launch notices
Actual posted XRP balances by account class
Net new spot acquisitions versus transfers of existing custody inventory

causal_hypotheses.thesis: Cross-collateral rebalancing can convert positive-equity XRP into a negative settlement currency, creating a potential mechanical XRP sell/conversion channel during account stress.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: No observed XRP rebalancing transactions or disclosed volume
Rebalancing is not liquidation and may be small relative to spot market depth
decisive_missing_data: Venue-level rebalancing volume by source asset
Time-aligned XRP order-book depth and price impact

causal_hypotheses.thesis: USDC and RLUSD may complement XRP by deepening XRPL settlement/liquidity while substituting for XRP as the bridge asset on some payment routes.
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: Native stablecoin availability does not establish payment routing or customer preference
XRP can remain useful for bridge liquidity and exchange inventory
decisive_missing_data: Route-level payment volumes and token paths
XRPL DEX and AMM liquidity changes

causal_hypotheses.thesis: Custody, listings, exchange support and collateral eligibility can expand utility without creating equivalent net spot demand because assets may be transferred, wrapped or rehypothecated from existing inventory.
supporting_evidence: cbXRP reserve accounting in prior ledger
disconfirming_or_limiting_evidence: Sustained net new inventory accumulation or measurable spot execution attributable to new use would weaken this hypothesis
decisive_missing_data: Custodian inventory changes adjusted for wrapped liabilities
Institutional spot executions and net exposure changes
